samples.text: Pending a permanent correction, the service runs on a workaround: manual agency code mapping override applied to complete valuation for the period. That basis is deliberate and provisional. The cause behind it is now confirmed as stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register, so the override corrects exactly the entry that failed and does not change anything else in the run. There is no budget or forecast for a measure of this kind. The fair comparison is with normal operation, where the mapping is applied without an engineer in the loop and the run needs no approval to proceed. Readers deciding whether to wait can rely on the current output for this period, because the override targets the confirmed fault rather than a guess. They must not treat it as a fix. Legacy and cloud agency codes are both in use and are not interchangeable, and until someone corrects the mapping at its source, every new run depends on the same manual step. The platform team will

The valuation failure has one established cause: stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. That finding is confirmed, and it replaces the explanation the team worked from at the start. Triage initially recorded the cause as overnight ERP outage, because an overnight batch had stopped with no clear error and an upstream interruption fitted the timing. The evidence did not support that view: ERP logs show no interruption during the valuation window. With the upstream system cleared, engineers moved to the agency code mapping and found the stale entry that the inventory valuation service could not resolve. The review then classified the root cause at the level of the control, as control failure: the mapping table has no registered owner and no required reviewer. A stale row is only the symptom. The real condition is a table that nobody is accountable for, so nobody noticed when one of its entries became out of date.
